title: Without the Fox Getting Drenched...!
paragraphs: The smithy forging implements for war it was Where soldiers from the army camp were at work. There came a young maiden running, holding a letter of palmyra leaf.

A warrior-hero engaged in the work exclaimed: “You are the woman who can bathe the fox without getting it wet! I presumed you would come tomorrow. But today just as I am making this sword, You have arrived to gladden my heart. What letter did my flower-eyed woman give? Give it!” So saying he received the letter Without minding the taunts and comments from those around.

The text of the letter ran: I expected your visit during daytime yesterday and waited with hunger; Then only I realized that all your assurances are like letters written on thin air. I even became apprehensive of a friend’s prediction that our love would fail.
Dear, if you are afraid of coming in broad daylight You can as well come lurking in the darkness of night.
Are you afraid of the wretched moon’s light? At dusk, once the sun vanishes you can plan your visit.
Obstacles may abound in thwarting your visit. But only you possess the medicine for my withering heart.
Even the flower I sport loses its fragrance in your absence. Have you not learnt the art of outwitting the local guards Who are active throughout the day?
The path you have to tread is full of stones and thorns I do know how difficult a path it is.

Maybe it is well That your journey is not taken keeping in mind the nature of the path. But it will be a pleasure for me If you were to come here to wipe the tears off my eyes. Many a time have we planned to meet, But on thinking we know it to be risky. And what remains is confusion.
Even our families have become apprehensive; As one alleviates one’s hunger without waiting for one’s turn, Rushing into marriage is the only way out.

Folding the palmyra letter, The hero gave a tender twist to the emissary’s ear. “I told you then itself that you can bathe the fox without getting it wet. Tell your friend I shall not fail my word. Let the month of Thai be born, A way out will have been born too,” he said.
The young woman responded, “A child would also be born in the tenth mouth.” She asked further, “What does bathing the fox without getting it wet mean?
I ask you out of ignorance. Please do let me know it.”
He replied, “The fox is none but me. You have brought the love letter from my love and showered me with happiness, Without getting me drenched in the process.”

> Pointing to the perils attendant on > The hero’s coming for union at inopportune time, > The hazards of the tract that he comes through, > The rigours of watch around, > Speaking of her anxiety and concern therein, > Expressing her apprehension of harm to the hero, > Changing the hour of trysting > From day to night and from night to day, > And instructing him not to come for trysting > Drawing on things righteous and evil > To bring her point home, > And things such as these [by the confidante] > Are all the ones marked with the intent > To see the hero take the heroine in marriage, > Thus has it been ruled.
